title: Trapping Rain Water
summary: Treat the array as adjacent columns of unit width.

contractDetails.constraints: The array has 1–20,000 heights in [0, 100,000]. Water can escape past either end.

statement: Treat the array as adjacent columns of unit width. After rainfall, a low column can hold water when taller columns block escape to both sides. Return the total number of unit squares of water above the columns.

examples.explanation: The inside columns hold 2 and 3 units.
Water flows out along the descending side.

constraints: The array has 1–20,000 heights in [0, 100,000]. Water can escape past either end.
hints: Conceptual: A column fills up to the lower of the highest walls on its two sides.
Directional: Track a maximum height seen from each end.
Implementation: Settle the side with the lower running maximum. Its water contribution is that maximum minus the current height after updating the maximum.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Each position is settled from one side.
